verdict.rationale: Luma documents its own camera-direction capability: Ray can transfer cinematic camera moves from a source video to new scenes. Multi-Keyframe adds beat-by-beat control over what changes and what holds. This gives creators a documented way to direct motion, but by reference footage and keyframes rather than explicit pan/zoom/orbit/static controls. Missing for 10: documented named camera-move controls (pan, zoom, orbit, static lock), prompt- or API-level camera parameters, and hands-on corroboration that directed camera moves are reliably followed.

support.subject: As a creator, I can direct camera moves (pan, zoom, orbit, static) instead of accepting whatever motion the model picks

citations.quote: Transfer cinematic camera moves across scenes, worlds, and styles.
Apply motion from a source video to new subjects, scenes, or styles.
Multi-Keyframe lets you set up to 16 keyframes inside a single clip. Direct what changes and what holds, beat by beat.
